Questions.answer: A small construction crew in Vavuniya.

activity_b.text: Good morning, please take a seat.
I’m Ms. Jayasuriya, the site training supervisor.
How are you feeling today?
Good morning, madam. I’m doing fine, thank you.
I’m a bit nervous, but I’m ready to try my best.
It’s alright, this is a friendly discussion.
So, Kavishan, I see you completed school last year.
Could you tell me a little about your background?
Yes, madam. I completed my A/Ls in August.
During my final year, I worked part-time with a small construction crew in Vavuniya.
I don’t have a lot of experience yet, but I can manage basic on-site tasks confidently.
That’s good.
What kind of work did you support at the site?
I assisted the masons with mixing cement, carrying bricks, and preparing mortar.
I also helped carpenters set up formwork and sometimes cleaned reinforcement bars before concrete pouring.
When the site became very busy, I talked to suppliers and checked the delivery lists.
I wasn’t responsible for major tasks, but I always supported the team whenever extra help was needed.
Excellent.
What skills do you think you can bring to our project team?
I can level surfaces carefully, madam.
I know how to measure distances accurately with a tape and spirit level.
I also learnt to stay calm when schedules get tight.
I might need some guidance with scaffolding assembly and reading full site drawings at the beginning, but I’m going to improve quickly.
That’s a positive attitude.
How comfortable are you with blocklaying and basic concrete work?
I’m not fully skilled yet, but I can already handle simple tasks like preparing the mix and supporting the masonry line.
I might take more time with complex structural work.
That’s understandable.
What are your plans for the next few years?
I’m going to complete this training programme and then apply for an apprenticeship.
I might also follow short NVQ courses so I can strengthen my technical skills.
Good plan.
Thank you, Kavishan. We’ll contact you soon.
Thank you very much, madam. I appreciate the opportunity.
